activities.title: Debit or credit?
activities.objective: Decide which side records an increase in each kind of account.
activities.scenario: Under the modern approach assets and expenses are increased by debits; liabilities, capital and incomes are increased by credits.
steps: Read each account and ask: is it an asset, liability, capital, expense or income?
Choose the side that records an INCREASE in it.
Press Check my work to see which are right.

items.why: Cash is an asset. Assets increase on the debit side.
A creditor is a liability. Liabilities increase on the credit side.
Capital is the owner's claim. It increases on the credit side.
Rent is an expense. Expenses increase on the debit side.
Sales are income. Income increases on the credit side.
Furniture is an asset, so the debit side records the increase.
Drawings reduce capital. A reduction in a credit-balance account is recorded as a debit.
Commission received is income, which increases on the credit side.

activities.title: Build a trial balance
activities.objective: Total the debit and credit columns of Rohan Stationers' trial balance and prove that they agree.
activities.scenario: At 30 April 2026 the ledger balances of Rohan Stationers are listed. A trial balance is correct only if total debits equal total credits.
steps: Click B9 and type =SUM(B2:B8), then press Enter.
Click C9 and total the credit column the same way.
Click B10 and type =B9-C9. A difference of 0 means the books agree.

checks.label: B9 totals the debit column with SUM
checks.hint: Type =SUM(B2:B8). The range B2:B8 runs from the first to the last debit balance.
checks.explain: The debit balances add up to 255000 + 140000 + 15000 + 10000 = 420000.

checks.label: C9 totals the credit column with SUM
checks.hint: Use the same idea for column C.
checks.explain: The credit balances add up to 300000 + 90000 + 30000 = 420000.

checks.label: B10 shows the difference as a formula
checks.hint: Type =B9-C9 so the cell updates if a balance changes.
checks.explain: 420000 - 420000 = 0. The trial balance agrees.

checks.label: No error messages anywhere
checks.hint: Read the red message under the cell to see what is wrong.
checks.explain: A formula error always has a reason: a missing bracket, a wrong cell name or text where a number should be.

activities.title: Straight-line vs written-down value
activities.objective: Build a three-year depreciation schedule for a machine under both methods using formulas.
activities.scenario: A machine costs 5,00,000 with scrap value 50,000 and a life of 5 years. WDV depreciation is 20%. Fill the schedule so it recalculates when the inputs change.
steps: B7: straight-line depreciation =(B1-B2)/B3. Copy the same idea to B8 and B9.
C7: book value =B1-B7. C8 =C7-B8, and so on.
D7: WDV depreciation =B1*B4. D8 uses the previous book value: =E7*B4.

checks.label: B7 is straight-line depreciation (cost - residual) / life
checks.hint: Type =(B1-B2)/B3.

checks.label: C9 is the SLM book value after three years
checks.hint: C9 should be C8 minus the third year's depreciation.

checks.label: D7 is year-1 WDV depreciation (rate x cost)
checks.hint: Type =B1*B4.

checks.label: D8 is year-2 WDV depreciation on the new book value
checks.hint: The rate applies to E7, the book value at the start of year 2.

checks.label: D9 is year-3 WDV depreciation
checks.hint: Rate times E8.

checks.label: E9 is the WDV book value after three years
No error messages anywhere
checks.hint: Read the red message under the cell to see what is wrong.
checks.explain: A formula error always has a reason: a missing bracket, a wrong cell name or text where a number should be.

activities.title: Value closing stock
activities.objective: Work out closing stock and cost of goods sold by weighted average and FIFO.
activities.scenario: Opening stock is 100 units at 50. On 10 January 200 units were bought at 55 and on 20 January 100 units at 60. 250 units were sold.
steps: Column D: total cost for each line, for example D2 =B2*C2.
B5 and D5: total units and total cost with SUM.
B8: closing units =B5-B7. B9: weighted average cost =D5/B5. B10: closing stock =B8*B9.
B11: FIFO closing stock. The 150 unsold units are the latest ones: 100 at 60 and 50 at 55.
B12: cost of goods sold under FIFO =D5-B11.

checks.label: D2 multiplies units by cost
checks.hint: Type =B2*C2.

checks.label: D5 totals the cost with SUM
checks.hint: Type =SUM(D2:D4).

checks.label: B5 totals the units with SUM
checks.hint: Type =SUM(B2:B4).
checks.explain: 100 + 200 + 100 = 400 units available.

checks.label: B8 gives closing units
checks.hint: Total available minus units sold.

checks.label: B9 is the weighted average cost per unit
checks.hint: Total cost divided by total units.

checks.label: B10 values closing stock at average cost
checks.hint: Closing units times the average cost.

checks.label: B11 values closing stock under FIFO
checks.hint: 100 units at 60 plus 50 units at 55.

checks.label: B12 is FIFO cost of goods sold
checks.hint: Total cost less FIFO closing stock.

checks.label: No error messages anywhere
checks.hint: Read the red message under the cell to see what is wrong.
checks.explain: A formula error always has a reason: a missing bracket, a wrong cell name or text where a number should be.

activities.title: Capital or revenue expenditure?
activities.objective: Tell spending that creates a long-term asset from spending that is used up in the year.
activities.scenario: Capital expenditure goes on the balance sheet as an asset. Revenue expenditure is charged to the profit and loss account this year.
steps: Ask: does the benefit last beyond this year, or does it improve what the business can do?
Choose Capital if yes, Revenue if no.
Press Check my work.

items.why: A van serves the business for years, so it is an asset.

items.text: Repairs to keep a machine running
items.why: Repairs maintain existing capacity and are used up in the year.

items.text: Wages paid to install a new machine
items.why: Installation is part of the cost of getting the machine ready for use.
Goods bought for resale are charged against sales.

items.text: Legal fees paid to buy land
items.why: Costs of acquiring an asset are added to its cost.
Salaries are a running cost of the year.

items.text: Major overhaul that extends a machine's life
items.why: It improves the asset beyond its original capacity.
Routine upkeep is consumed in the year.

activities.title: Prepare Meera Garments' accounts
activities.objective: Work out gross profit and net profit from the adjusted figures of Meera Garments.
activities.scenario: The year-end adjustments (outstanding salaries, prepaid insurance, depreciation and provision) are already included in the expenses listed. Complete the trading and profit and loss calculation.
steps: B20: net sales =B2-B3. B21: net purchases =B4-B5.
B22: cost of goods sold = opening stock + net purchases + wages + carriage inwards - closing stock.
B23: gross profit =B20-B22.
B24: total expenses with =SUM(B10:B17).
B25: net profit = gross profit + commission earned - total expenses.

checks.label: B20 is net sales (sales less returns)
checks.hint: Type =B2-B3.

checks.label: B21 is net purchases
checks.hint: Purchases less purchase returns.

checks.label: B22 is cost of goods sold
checks.hint: Opening stock + net purchases + wages + carriage inwards - closing stock.

checks.label: B23 is gross profit
checks.hint: Net sales less cost of goods sold.

checks.label: B24 totals the expenses with SUM
checks.hint: Type =SUM(B10:B17).

checks.label: B25 is net profit
checks.hint: Gross profit plus commission earned, less total expenses.

checks.label: No error messages anywhere
checks.hint: Read the red message under the cell to see what is wrong.
checks.explain: A formula error always has a reason: a missing bracket, a wrong cell name or text where a number should be.

activities.title: Ratio dashboard for Kiran Foods
activities.objective: Compute liquidity, profitability, activity and solvency ratios from the statements.
activities.scenario: Use the figures of Kiran Foods Ltd. (2025-26) to build a small ratio dashboard a banker could read.
steps: B13: current ratio =B6/B8.
B14: quick ratio =(B6-B7)/B8.
B15 and B16: gross profit and net profit as a share of net sales.
B17: debtors collection period in days =365/(B2/B11).
B18: debt-equity =B10/B9. B19: interest cover =(B4+B5)/B5. B20: return on equity =B4/B9.

checks.label: Current ratio is 1.8
checks.hint: Current assets divided by current liabilities.

checks.label: Quick ratio excludes stock
checks.hint: (Current assets - stock) / current liabilities.

checks.label: Gross profit % is 30%
checks.hint: (Net sales - COGS) / net sales.

checks.label: Net profit % is 10%
checks.hint: Net profit / net sales.

checks.label: Collection period is 36.5 days
checks.hint: 365 divided by debtors turnover (sales / debtors).
checks.explain: Turnover 10 times, so 365 / 10 = 36.5 days.

checks.label: Debt-equity ratio is 0.6
checks.hint: Long-term loan / shareholders' funds.

checks.label: Interest cover is 7 times
checks.hint: EBIT (profit + interest) / interest.

checks.label: Return on equity is 24%
checks.hint: Net profit / shareholders' funds.

checks.label: No error messages anywhere
checks.hint: Read the red message under the cell to see what is wrong.
checks.explain: A formula error always has a reason: a missing bracket, a wrong cell name or text where a number should be.

activities.title: GST on a purchase and a sale
activities.objective: Calculate input GST, output GST and the net amount payable.
activities.scenario: A registered trader buys goods for 1,00,000 and sells goods for 1,50,000, all within one state. GST is 18% on both (the rate is illustrative).
steps: B5: input GST =B1*B3.
B6: output GST =B2*B3.
B7: net payable =B6-B5.
B8: the CGST half of the net payable. B9: the amount the customer pays.

checks.label: Input GST is 18,000
checks.hint: Purchases times the GST rate.

checks.label: Output GST is 27,000
checks.hint: Sales times the GST rate.

checks.label: Net payable is 9,000
checks.hint: Output GST less input GST.

checks.label: CGST payable is 4,500
checks.hint: Half of the net payable (the other half is SGST).

checks.label: The customer pays 1,77,000
checks.hint: Sale plus output GST.

checks.label: No error messages anywhere
checks.hint: Read the red message under the cell to see what is wrong.
checks.explain: A formula error always has a reason: a missing bracket, a wrong cell name or text where a number should be.

activities.title: Reconcile the bank balance
activities.objective: Prepare a bank reconciliation statement and find the balance the bank shows.
activities.scenario: On 31 March 2026 the cash book bank column shows a debit balance of 85,000. Bank charges of 500 and a customer's direct deposit of 6,000 appear only in the pass book. Cheques of 12,000 were issued but not yet presented, and cheques of 8,000 were deposited but not yet credited.
steps: B7: correct the cash book first =B1-B2+B3.
B8: reach the pass book balance =B7+B4-B5.

checks.label: B7 is the adjusted cash book balance
checks.hint: Deduct the bank charges and add the direct deposit.

checks.label: B8 is the pass book balance
checks.hint: Add cheques issued but not presented, deduct cheques deposited but not credited.

checks.label: No error messages anywhere
checks.hint: Read the red message under the cell to see what is wrong.
checks.explain: A formula error always has a reason: a missing bracket, a wrong cell name or text where a number should be.
